topics.title: Cost segregation electrical component evidence
topics.trigger: A study identifies electrical costs but source documents do not explain the equipment or areas served.
topics.principle: Identify the function, location and relationship to the building or equipment before technical classification. The word electrical does not establish an asset class or recovery period.
topics.example: A warehouse has general lighting, tenant office wiring and a separate circuit serving production equipment.

topics.title: Cost segregation plumbing function records
topics.trigger: Plumbing invoices combine general building services and connections associated with particular equipment.
topics.principle: Separate the actual function and supported cost of each material component. Pipe location or vendor terminology alone does not decide the tax classification.
topics.example: A restaurant build-out includes restrooms, food preparation connections and equipment-specific plumbing on one contractor invoice.

topics.title: Cost segregation HVAC service boundaries
topics.trigger: A mechanical system serves spaces with different uses and ownership arrangements.
topics.principle: Document locations served and the system's actual purpose. A specialty use does not by itself make the entire mechanical system shorter-life property.
topics.example: A mixed-use building has a common system plus dedicated cooling for an equipment room.

topics.title: Cost segregation flooring installation facts
topics.trigger: A report identifies floor coverings while installation and replacement records are incomplete.
topics.principle: Record material, attachment, location and actual cost. Different products and circumstances can require different analysis; do not infer classification from a generic flooring label.
topics.example: A furnished rental replaces carpeting in some rooms and installs a different hard surface in others.

topics.title: Cost segregation cabinetry function records
topics.trigger: A contractor invoice covers built-in storage and equipment-related fixtures.
topics.principle: Identify the actual use, installation and relationship to the building or business equipment. A custom-built item is not automatically classified in one category.
topics.example: A medical office build-out includes reception cabinets, general storage and cabinetry serving specialized treatment functions.

topics.title: Cost segregation signage source files
topics.trigger: Signage costs include multiple types of signs and installation work.
topics.principle: Separate sign components, supporting structures and actual use for technical review. One marketing label does not resolve classification or cost allocation.
topics.example: A property owner buys interior wayfinding signs, exterior tenant signage and an entrance monument under one contract.

topics.title: Cost segregation site drainage mapping
topics.trigger: A property project includes drains serving buildings and exterior areas.
topics.principle: Document where water is collected and discharged and what each component serves. Site-related terminology alone does not establish the tax treatment of all costs.
topics.example: An industrial property has roof drainage, parking area drains and new exterior stormwater work on a shared plan.

topics.title: Cost segregation parking project reconciliation
topics.trigger: Parking work combines paving, grading, lighting and repairs.
topics.principle: Separate the project components and support the cost pool. A single parking contract may include items requiring different analysis and prior-history review.
topics.example: An owner repaves part of a lot, adds lighting and improves drainage while another part remains unchanged.

topics.title: Cost segregation fencing and gate evidence
topics.trigger: A site has perimeter fencing, controlled entry and other barriers with different functions.
topics.principle: Identify physical components, location and use before technical classification. Security equipment and supporting structures need supported cost and ownership information.
topics.example: A self-storage site replaces some fencing and installs powered gates without a clean division in the vendor invoice.

topics.title: Cost segregation landscaping cost boundaries
topics.trigger: Exterior invoices combine plants, irrigation, grading and routine care.
topics.principle: Distinguish newly acquired or installed components from recurring services and unrelated work. Landscaping is a broad label rather than a complete cost classification.
topics.example: An owner pays one contractor to install new irrigation, reshape an area and provide monthly maintenance.

topics.title: Cost segregation tenant improvement ownership
topics.trigger: An improvement project involves landlord contributions, tenant payments and lease obligations.
topics.principle: Identify the agreements and payer, owner and user facts. A construction invoice alone does not determine which taxpayer includes a component in a study.
topics.example: A commercial tenant receives an allowance, pays additional construction costs and installs its own equipment.

topics.title: Cost segregation contractor allowances
topics.trigger: A construction contract includes estimated allowances later adjusted by selections and change orders.
topics.principle: Reconcile final installed work and costs rather than relying on original allowances. Deposits, credits and direct purchases can change the source pool.
topics.example: A builder's contract contains fixture allowances but the owner selects more expensive items and buys some directly.

topics.title: Cost segregation demolition and retained structure
topics.trigger: A project removes part of a property while retaining other elements.
topics.principle: Map what was removed, retained and newly constructed. Demolition, disposition and new construction treatment require factual and tax review beyond a study estimate.
topics.example: A rental renovation removes interior work while retaining the structure and several existing systems.

topics.title: Cost segregation construction soft costs
topics.trigger: Project costs include design, permits, oversight and other indirect amounts.
topics.principle: Keep the source costs and allocation method visible. Indirect costs should not vanish from the total or be assigned solely to maximize a desired deduction.
topics.example: A new rental project has architect, permit and construction management invoices separate from the builder's contract.

topics.title: Cost segregation quantity estimate confidence
topics.trigger: A study relies on estimated quantities because complete plans are unavailable.
topics.principle: Record the source, measurement method and limitations of each material quantity. An estimate should not be presented as an exact observed measurement.
topics.example: A remote study uses photographs and partial drawings to estimate components in several areas that have not been measured.

topics.title: Cost segregation cost estimate source dates
topics.trigger: A report uses cost data that may reflect a different date or scope from the property project.
topics.principle: Identify the estimate source, date, location and adjustment method. Estimated replacement cost does not automatically equal the taxpayer's historical cost basis.
topics.example: An older rental has few invoices, and a provider develops an estimate using current cost information and documented adjustments.

topics.title: Cost segregation source pool exclusions
topics.trigger: Several items appear in the source file but may fall outside the study scope.
topics.principle: Identify excluded amounts and why they are excluded. The study total should reconcile to the accepted source pool rather than silently dropping unexplained amounts.
topics.example: A project source list includes land, financing charges, owner furnishings and unrelated operating expenses.

topics.title: Cost segregation component identifier continuity
topics.trigger: A property has report revisions, replacement purchases and several asset schedules.
topics.principle: Use stable component references or a documented mapping between versions. A renamed report row should not create a duplicate asset or erase its history.
topics.example: A provider revises room names while the preparer's asset software still uses identifiers from the first report.

topics.title: Cost segregation report to return reconciliation
topics.trigger: A study is delivered but the owner does not know how it affected the tax return.
topics.principle: Document the preparer's accepted cost, classification and reporting treatment. Report delivery, asset software entry and filed return implementation are separate milestones.
topics.example: An owner receives a final PDF, while the preparer asks about prior elections and a possible accounting-method procedure.

topics.title: Cost segregation replacement and sale archive
topics.trigger: A property changes after the original study and later may be sold.
topics.principle: Preserve additions, removals and report revisions together with the actual tax schedules. An initial estimate does not provide a complete later disposition analysis.
topics.example: An investor replaces appliances and a gate, then sells the property several years after receiving a study.
